# Filter Coffee
Filter coffee uses a 1:16 ratio of coffee to water.
## Pour over
- Rinse the paper filter.
- Bloom with twice the coffee weight in water for 30 seconds.
- Pour in slow circles until the target weight.
Colombian lots from ![[origins]] are the default filter offering. The grinder setting is described in [grinders](dizin%20adı/grinders.md).

# Roasting
Roasting turns green coffee into the brown beans we grind. The roaster controls heat, airflow and time, and every batch is logged in [[roast-log#Roast Log]].
## Stages
1. Drying: moisture leaves the bean until it turns yellow.
2. Maillard: sugars and amino acids react and aromas develop. - The bean expands and the color moves to tan. - Most body is built here.
3. Development: the time after first crack that sets acidity.
## Profiles
Light profiles keep floral notes and are used for [[origins|Ethiopian lots]]. Dark profiles mute acidity and suit [[espresso|espresso notu]].
> Never roast two origins in the same drum without a cleaning cycle.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.

# Maintenance
Regular maintenance keeps the equipment safe.
## Daily
- Backflush the espresso machine with a blind basket.
- Empty the chaff collector of the roaster.
## Monthly
- Descale the espresso machine boiler.
- Inspect the roaster exhaust for build-up.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.

# Roasting
Roasting turns green coffee into the brown beans we grind. The roaster controls heat, airflow and time, and every batch is logged in [[r034-r029-r021-r013-r011-r006-roast-log#Roast Log]].
## Stages
1. Drying: moisture leaves the bean until it turns yellow.
2. Maillard: sugars and amino acids react and aromas develop. - The bean expands and the color moves to tan. - Most body is built here.
3. Development: the time after first crack that sets acidity.
## Profiles
Light profiles keep floral notes and are used for [[r035-r033-origins|Ethiopian lots]]. Dark profiles mute acidity and suit [[espresso|espresso notu]].
> Never roast two origins in the same drum without a cleaning cycle.
Note: always check the drum temperature before charging.

# Cupping
Cupping is the standard tasting protocol used to evaluate lots.
## Protocol
1. Grind 8.25 g of coffee per 150 ml of water.
2. Smell the dry grounds.
3. Pour water at 93 °C and wait four minutes.
4. Break the crust and skim.
5. Slurp from a spoon and score.
## Scoring

Scores cover fragrance, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body and balance. Lots under 84 points are rejected. Results are stored next to the [roast-log hakkında](r034-r029-r021-r013-r011-r006-roast-log.md).

# Cupping
Cupping is the standard tasting protocol used to evaluate lots.
## Protocol
1. Grind 8.25 g of coffee per 150 ml of water.
2. Smell the dry grounds.
3. Pour water at 93 °C and wait four minutes.
4. Break the crust and skim.
5. Slurp from a spoon and score.
## Scoring

Scores cover fragrance, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body and balance. Lots under 84 points are rejected. Results are stored next to the [roast-log hakkında](r034-r029-r021-r013-r011-r006-roast-log.md).

Burr grinders give a consistent particle size. Flat burrs are used for [[r048-r047-r039-espresso]] and conical burrs for filter.

Grind size is adjusted daily. A finer grind slows the shot, a coarser grind speeds it up.
## Cleaning
Grinders are cleaned weekly with rice-free cleaning tablets.
